newsitem.title: FRANCE: Explosive charge fails outside Corsican bank.
newsitem.headline: Explosive charge fails outside Corsican bank.

text.p: An explosive charge made up of three sticks of dynamite failed to go off after being placed overnight outside a bank in the central Corsican town of Sartene, police said on Saturday.
There was no indication of who was responsible but Corsican separatists were suspected.

Six suspected separatist militants who were flown to Paris after being arrested in Corsica during the week were placed under investigation late on Friday evening by a magistrate specialised in terrorism cases.

They were advised they were being investigated for suspected membership of a terrorist group and offences against weapons laws. A seventh man was released on condition that he report his whereabouts regularly to police.
Justice sources said the seven were connected to the A Cuncolta Naziunalista party, legal facade of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC).
They are suspected of involvement in the machinegunning of a hotel in the town of Aregno in October, the sources said. The FLNC has claimed responsibility for the attack.
